01 — Framework

Three directions.
All genuinely different.

Each direction represents a distinct visual and verbal approach to Pawside. The three directions are not color variations of the same concept — they are three fundamentally different aesthetic and strategic choices. Each direction is designed to work for Maya and for a dog owner in the premium segment, but each owns a different brand personality.

Direction A (Warmth / Golden Hour) leads with emotional connection and dog-as-hero photography. Direction B (Precision / Laboratory) leads with ingredient transparency and clinical credibility. Direction C (Minimal / Sacred) combines dog photography with extreme minimalism and reverence for the dog-owner bond.

A
Warmth
Golden Hour · Dog Hero · Emotional

Direction A leads with the dog owner's emotional connection. The visual language is warm, golden-hour photography. Dogs are shot in natural light outdoors, with their owners visible in the frame. The palette is warm (cream, rust, amber, sage) with prominent gold accents. Typography is serif-forward (Cormorant Garamond) with generous spacing. The feeling is aspirational warmth — not clinical, not minimal, but deeply felt.

Three-column analysis

Feeling
Warm, emotional, aspirational. The dog owner's love is visible on every page.
Who it appeals to
Emotional dog owners. Instagram-first buyers. People who see their dog as a family member first.
The risk
Can read as saccharine if not executed carefully. Competes directly with The Farmer's Dog on emotional territory.

B
Precision
Laboratory · Data · Science-First

Direction B leads with ingredient transparency and scientific credibility. The visual language is clinical but elegant — product close-ups, ingredient percentages as design elements, charts showing ingredient benefits. The palette is cool (cream, stone, dark navy, sage). Typography is sans-serif forward (DM Sans) with monospace for ingredient data. The feeling is precise, trustworthy, and research-backed.

Three-column analysis

Feeling
Clinical, trustworthy, researched. The data speaks for itself. No emotional manipulation.
Who it appeals to
Science-first buyers. People who verify everything. Data-driven decision makers.
The risk
Can read as cold and corporate. May underestimate the emotional dog-owner bond. Competes with Ollie's science positioning.
C
Sacred
Minimal · Reverent · Dog-Centered

Direction C is the synthesis. Extreme minimalism meets dog reverence. The visual language strips everything non-essential. Each image is carefully composed: the dog is the subject, the background is simple, white space is generous. Ingredient percentages are present but integrated subtly. The palette is reduced (cream, stone, rust accents only). Typography is minimal and elegant. The feeling is that this brand understands the sacred relationship between dog and owner.

Three-column analysis

Feeling
Reverent, minimal, intentional. Every element earns its place. The dog and the formula are sacred.
Who it appeals to
Thoughtful, intentional dog owners. People who see minimalism as a virtue. Design-literate buyers.
The risk
Can feel cold if the dog photography is not exceptional. Requires the most careful art direction. Most difficult to execute well.

D
Playful
Vibrant · Dog Joy · Community-First

Direction D leans into the joy and playfulness of dog ownership. The visual language is vibrant, colorful, and celebration-focused. Dogs are caught mid-play, mid-joy, mid-personality. The palette introduces brighter, more saturated colors alongside the warm tones — coral, teal, sunny yellow accents. Typography mixes serif and sans-serif playfully. User-generated content and real dog owner moments dominate. The feeling is that Pawside is part of a joyful community of dog lovers, not a clinical brand but a friend.

Three-column analysis

Feeling
Joyful, playful, celebratory. This brand gets how much dogs mean to us. Part friend, part guide.
Who it appeals to
Community-first dog owners. People who post dog content. Younger millennial buyers. Dog lovers who want to celebrate, not just solve problems.
The risk
Can read as less premium or less serious about science. May compete directly with Nom Nom's playful positioning. Risks being perceived as "cute" rather than "quality."

02 — Direction lock
Direction Selected
C — Sacred
Minimal · Reverent · Dog-Centered
Direction C owns the unclaimed intersection. Warmth (Direction A) competes with The Farmer's Dog on emotional territory. Precision (Direction B) competes with Ollie on scientific territory. Sacred (Direction C) — the combination of reverent minimalism with ingredient transparency and dog-as-subject photography — is claimed by no competitor in the premium pet care market. This is Pawside's position.

Why C over A and B: Direction A is visually beautiful but emotionally redundant (The Farmer's Dog already owns this). Direction B is strategically sound but aesthetically cold. Direction C combines the best of both — dog reverence from A, transparency from B, and a visual system that feels completely distinct from every competitor. It is the most ambitious direction. It is also the most differentiated.
